decisions.reason: As a core airfield-control product launched with visible web promotion and tied to the firm's integrated automation direction, management is likely to continue it and treat any weaker demand as temporary.

This surveillance display fits the firm's established systems business and public strategic move toward real-time information sharing, so sunk development effort and strategic commitment favor persistence.
Although training is easier to scale back than hardware, the dedicated launch and its support role for installed systems make management more likely to retain it than abandon it.

This narrower training course had the weakest visible commitment and likely the lowest dedicated investment, so it is the easiest offering to remove if management reallocates resources despite its tendency to persist.
An airport collaboration software tool is highly central to the firm's stated future of collaborative, data-driven airport operations, which makes management especially prone to continue backing it.

A multilateration surveillance system likely required substantial R&D and fits the firm's integrated airport solutions portfolio, so management would be reluctant to withdraw it and may blame disappointing results on temporary market conditions.
